name: Ramen-CHORD-Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid gated linear attention (Gated DeltaNet) in parallel with full GQA attention every 4th layer; 12 of 48 layers are full attention
notes: ADDED 2026-11-02. CHORD (GRPO with on-the-fly SFT mixed into the rollout loop) applied to Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct by the Ramen Team (University of Tokyo / NEDO JPNP25006 medical-LLM programme). Deterministic RL fine-tune, not a merge or a quant: config.json is the base's field for field (2048 hidden, 48 layers, 512 experts, 10 per token, 262144 ctx, 12 full-attention layers of 48), and the safetensors index reports 79,674,391,296 parameters BF16 - a single-shard complete set, versus the base record's rounded 80B label. KV cache (24576 B/token) and active-parameter figures are inherited unchanged, and so is flops_per_token_active (6.0e9) - the two records describe the same 3B-active geometry, so a different FLOP figure in a derivative would be an arithmetic claim about the base, not about this checkpoint. The generator's 6x-active default was overridden to the base's own 2x-active value for that reason; see the PR body for why the catalog carries both conventions. Trained with ms-swift + Megatron-LM v3.9.3. Recorded because the card prints base and CHORD columns in the SAME table on two Japanese medical MCQ benchmarks, and CHORD is higher on all four rows. THREE CAVEATS the card states itself and which the rows carry: (1) the card reports McNemar p=0.282 on igakuqa and p=0.119 on specialist_exam_test_v2 - both wins are statistically insignificant, +0.9 and +1.0 points on 1,122 and 3,757 items; (2) the card names a known confound it believes suppresses the RL gain, namely that the SFT data is natural-language structured answers while both the RL reward and the eval are MCQ; (3) the model is an explicit research artefact - the card says it has had no clinical safety validation, is not for clinical use, and did not run J-HealthBench, Do-Not-Answer or AnswerCarefully. Read the numbers as a method-comparison datapoint inside one project (GRPO vs GSPO vs CHORD on one base), not as a leaderboard entry. Sibling variants (Ramen-GRPO, Ramen-GSPO, and two Pinpoint-Tuning models on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507) are not recorded here. Licence apache-2.0, repo created 2026-03-03.

benchmarks.name: igakuqa
benchmarks.config: Card table igakuqa (Japanese medical licensing exam, 2023-2025, N=1,122): column 'base' 89.5% vs 'this model' 90.4% (+0.9). MCQ accuracy, all items, 0-shot. Bootstrap 95% CI base [87.6, 91.3] vs CHORD [88.7, 92.2]; McNemar 40 improved / 30 worsened, p=0.282 - the card states the difference is NOT significant.

benchmarks.name: igakuqa (text-only subset)
benchmarks.config: Same table, row 'Accuracy (subset, text only)': base 93.6% vs CHORD 94.1% (+0.5). Subset excludes the image-bearing items; the card does not give N for the subset.

benchmarks.name: specialist_exam_test_v2
benchmarks.config: Card table specialist_exam_test_v2 (13 specialties, N=3,757): base 69.0% vs CHORD 70.0% (+1.0). MCQ accuracy, all items. CI base [67.5, 70.4] vs CHORD [68.5, 71.6]; McNemar 317 improved / 278 worsened, p=0.119 - the card states NOT significant.

benchmarks.name: specialist_exam_test_v2 (text-only subset)
benchmarks.config: Same table, row 'Accuracy (subset, text only)': base 73.0% vs CHORD 73.9% (+0.9). Text-only subset of the 13-specialty set.
